title: What we really teach women and boys
source_text: Ὅρα δὴ καὶ ἐν τούτοις, τίνα τρόπον διασύρων τοὺς παρ᾿ ἡμῖν διδάσκοντας τὸν λόγον καὶ ἐπὶ τὸν τῶν ὅλων δημιουργὸν παντὶ τρόπῳ τὴν ψυχὴν ἀναβιβάζειν πειρωμένους, παριστάντας δὲ καὶ ὡς χρὴ μὲν τῶν αἰσθητῶν καὶ προσκαίρων καὶ βλεπομένων πάντων καταφρονεῖν πάντα δὲ πράττειν ὑπὲρ τοῦ τυχεῖν τῆς τοῦ θεοῦ κοινωνίας καὶ τῆς τῶν νοητῶν καὶ ἀοράτων θεωρίας καὶ μακαρίας μετὰ θεοῦ καὶ τῶν οἰκείων τοῦ θεοῦ διεξαγωγῆς, παραβάλλει αὐτοὺς τοῖς κατὰ τὰς οἰκίας ἐριουργοῖς καὶ τοῖς σκυτοτόμοις καὶ τοῖς κναφεῦσι καὶ τοῖς ἀγροικοτάτοις τῶν ἀνθρώπων, ἐπὶ τὰ φαῦλα προκαλουμένους παῖδας κομιδῇ νηπίους καὶ γύναια. ἵν᾿ ἀποστῶσι μὲν πατρὸς καὶ διδασκάλων αὐτοῖς δὲ ἕπωνται. τίνος γὰρ πατρὸς σωφρονοῦντος ἢ τίνων διδασκάλων σεμνότερα διδασκόντων ἀφίσταμεν τοὺς παῖδας καὶ τὰ γύναια, παραστησάτω ὁ Κέλσος καὶ ἀντιπαραβαλέτω ἐπὶ τῶν προσιόντων τῷ λόγῳ ἡμῶν παίδων καὶ γυναίων, πότερά τινα ὧν ἤκουν βελτίονα τῶν ἡμετέρων. καὶ τίνα τρόπον καλῶν τινων καὶ σεμνῶν μαθημάτων ἀφιστάντες παῖδας καὶ γύναια ἐπὶ τὰ χείρονα προκαλούμεθα. ἀλλ᾿ οὐχ ἕξει παραστῆσαι τὸ τοιοῦτο καθ᾿ ἡμῶν· τοὐναντίον γὰρ τὰ μὲν γύναια ἀκολασίας καὶ διαστροφῆς τῆς ἀπὸ τῶν συνόντων ἀφίσταμεν καὶ πάσης θεατρομανίας καὶ ὀρχηστομανίας καὶ δεισιδαιμονίας. τοὺς δὲ παῖδας ἄρτι ἡβῶντας καὶ σφριγῶντας ταῖς περὶ τὰ ἀφροδίσια ὀρέξεσι σωφρονίζομεν, παρατιθέντες οὐ μόνον τὸ ἐν τοῖς ἁμαρτανομένοις αἰσχρὸν ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐν οἷς ἔσται διὰ τὰ τοιαῦτα ἡ τῶν φαύλων ψυχὴ, καὶ οἵας τίσει δίκας καὶ ὡς κολασθήσεται.
pass_a_gloss: See (ὁράω) also in these how, disparaging (διασύρω) those among us teaching the word (λόγος) and trying (πειράομαι) in every way to lead up (ἀναβιβάζω) the soul (ψυχή) to the Creator (δημιουργός) of the whole (τὰ ὅλα), and presenting (παρίστημι) that one must despise (καταφρονέω) all things sensible (αἰσθητός), temporary (πρόσκαιρος) and seen (βλέπω), and do everything for attaining (τυγχάνω) fellowship (κοινωνία) of God and contemplation (θεωρία) of intelligible (νοητός) and invisible (ἀόρατος) things and the blessed (μακάριος) life/conduct (διεξαγωγή) with God and those belonging (οἰκεῖος) to God, he compares (παραβάλλω) them to the wool-workers in houses and cobblers and fullers and the most boorish of men, calling (προκαλέομαι) to base things (τὰ φαῦλα) children quite (κομιδῇ) infant (νήπιος) and little women, so that they stand away (ἀφίστημι) from father and teachers but follow (ἕπομαι) them. For from what father being sober (σωφρονέω), or what teachers teaching more dignified things, do we draw away the children and the women? Let Celsus present (παρίστημι) and compare in turn, regarding children and women coming to our word (λόγος), whether any of what they heard (ἀκούω, impf.) [was] better than ours, and in what way, drawing children and women from fine (καλός) and dignified lessons (μάθημα), we call them to worse (χείρων). But he will not have [power] to present such a thing against us; for, on the contrary, we draw the women away from licentiousness (ἀκολασία) and the perversion (διαστροφή) from those they live with (σύνειμι), and every mania for theatres (θεατρομανία) and dancing (ὀρχηστομανία) and superstition; and the boys just coming of age (ἡβάω) and swelling (σφριγάω) with the desires (ὄρεξις) for sex (τὰ ἀφροδίσια) we make self-controlled (σωφρονίζω), setting before them (παρατίθημι) not only the shamefulness (τὸ αἰσχρόν) in sins (ἁμαρτάνω) but also in what [state] the soul of the base will be through such things, and what penalties (δίκη) it will pay (τίνω) and how it will be punished (κολάζω).
pass_b_english: See, then, in this passage too, how he mocks those among us who teach the word and try in every way to raise the soul up to the Creator of the universe, who show that one must despise all things that are perceived by the senses, temporary and seen (compare 2 Corinthians 4:18), and must do everything in order to attain fellowship with God, the contemplation of things intelligible and invisible, and a blessed life with God and with those who belong to God; and how he compares them to the wool-workers in houses, and to the cobblers and fullers and the most boorish of men, as men who invite children, mere infants, and women to base things, so that they will abandon father and teachers and follow them.

From what sober-minded father, or from what teachers of nobler things, do we draw away children and women? Let Celsus show it; and in the case of the children and women who come to our teaching, let him set side by side and compare whether any of the things they used to hear was better than ours, and in what way we draw children and women away from fine and noble studies and invite them to worse ones. But he will not be able to show any such thing against us. On the contrary, we draw women away from licentiousness and from the perversion that comes from their companions, and from all mad love of theatres and dancing, and from superstition; and the boys who are just reaching manhood and swelling with sexual desires we bring to self-control, setting before them not only the shamefulness that lies in these sins, but also the state in which the soul of the wicked will be because of such things, what penalties it will pay, and how it will be punished.

choices.choice: τῶν αἰσθητῶν καὶ προσκαίρων καὶ βλεπομένων … τῆς τῶν νοητῶν καὶ ἀοράτων θεωρίας echoes 2 Corinthians 4:18 (τὰ βλεπόμενα πρόσκαιρα), cited inline with ‘compare’ because it is an allusion, not a quotation. τοὺς … διδάσκοντας τὸν λόγον: ‘the word’ = the Christian message, lowercase. ‘Mere infants and women’ keeps Origen’s summary of Celsus’s charge without quotation marks, since Origen is paraphrasing, not quoting. σωφρονίζομεν rendered ‘bring to self-control’.
προκαλουμένους (acc., agreeing with αὐτούς): ‘as though they invited’ added a ‘pretence’ sense not in the Greek; now ‘as men who invite children, mere infants, and women’
τὸ ἐν τοῖς ἁμαρτανομένοις αἰσχρόν: ‘such sins’ to ‘these sins’ (no τοιαῦτα in the Greek)
2 Corinthians 4:18 allusion checked (βλεπόμενα πρόσκαιρα); kept with ‘compare’
